newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Two injured, two missing in Singapore tanker fire.
newsitem.headline: Two injured, two missing in Singapore tanker fire.

text.p: Two crew members were injured and two other missing after a fire on board an oil product tanker in Singapore harbour, the Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) of Singapore said on Thursday.

The fire on board the 26,909-dwt Ocean Trader broke out at 6.20 p.m. (1020 GMT) on Wednesday while the Singapore-registered vessel was berthed at an oil terminal operated by U.S. oil company Mobil Corp on a small offshore island.
The fire was brought under control at 7.45 p.m. (1145 GMT), the MPA said in a statement.
Two of the tanker's crew were injured and evacuated to hospital. A further two crew members were reported missing, the MPA said.
A Mobil spokesman said the two missing crew members were believed to be Chinese nationals.
The company said the ship was discharging condensate, a type of light crude oil, to the Mobil refinery when the incident occured.
The cause of the fire was unknown.
The Mobil refinery is the second largest in Singapore, behind the Shell group, which operates a 430,000 bpd refinery. Singapore's overall refinery capacity is 1.245 million bpd.
The cause of the fire was unknown.
